title: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
summary: A one-arm pulldown that lets each lat work through a longer range than with a bar.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: lat pulldown station (seat and thigh pad) or cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.3 for traps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly traps total.

setup.text: Kneel or sit under a high pulley and take one handle.
Pull your elbow down to your side, rotating your palm in a little.
Reach fully back up to stretch the lat.

form_cues.cue: Pull the elbow down toward your hip
Reach fully up on the return
Lean a little toward the working side at the top to deepen the stretch.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Less stable, Both sides together.

notes: Ratings, swap attributes and cues are the library model (modeled). An authored page will replace this one.
